record.paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
record.original_question: Let (M, ∇, h) be an n-dimensional statistical manifold, fix a point p in M, and on a ∇-convex neighborhood U of p define, for each q in U \ {p}, a rank-(n−1) distribution D_q as the h-orthogonal complement of the velocity vector at q of the ∇-geodesic joining p to q in U. If every distribution D defined in this way is integrable, must the dual statistical manifold (M, ∇̄, h) be 1-conformally flat?

evidence.quote: We take an arbitrary point p of an n-dimensional statistical manifold (M, ∇, h) and define a distribution D of rank (n − 1) on a ∇-convex neighbourhood U of p as follows: for a point q of U\{p}, D_q is the h-orthogonal complement of the velocity vector at q of ∇-geodesic joining p and q in U. Is it true that the dual statistical manifold (M, ∇̄, h) is 1-conformally flat if every distribution D defined in this way is integrable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (M, ∇, h) be an n-dimensional statistical manifold; that is, M is a smooth n-manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric h and a torsion-free affine connection ∇ such that the (0,3)-tensor ∇h is totally symmetric. Let ∇̄ denote the dual connection of ∇ with respect to h, defined by

   X h(Y,Z) = h(∇_X Y, Z) + h(Y, ∇̄_X Z)

for all vector fields X, Y, Z on M. Recall that a statistical manifold (M, ∇, h) is called 1-conformally flat if there exists a smooth function φ on M such that, locally, the connection ∇ is projectively related, via the conformal change h̃ = e^{2φ} h together with a suitable projective change determined by dφ, to a flat connection — equivalently, the dual statistical structure is realized as a non-degenerate centroaffine immersion into affine space with parallel cubic form up to the standard 1-conformal transformation.

Fix a point p ∈ M and let U ⊂ M be a ∇-convex neighborhood of p, meaning that for every q ∈ U there is a unique ∇-geodesic in U joining p to q. For each q ∈ U \ {p}, let γ_q : [0,1] → U denote the ∇-geodesic with γ_q(0) = p and γ_q(1) = q, and define the rank-(n−1) distribution D on U \ {p} by

   D_q := { v ∈ T_q M : h(v, γ̇_q(1)) = 0 }.

Question: If, for every choice of p ∈ M and every ∇-convex neighborhood U of p, the distribution D constructed above on U \ {p} is involutive (i.e. integrable in the sense of Frobenius), does it follow that the dual statistical manifold (M, ∇̄, h) is 1-conformally flat?

The problem appears to remain open, but no definitive recent reference confirming its status was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses 1-conformally flat statistical manifolds and their relation to Hessian domains, but does not address the integrability-of-D criterion.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on 1-conformal flatness exists, but no resolution of the stated criterion was found.
